The judge ruled that Apple's compensation disclosures met securities law requirements and found no proof of improper actions by the board, also noting the plaintiffs did not allow sufficient time for the board to address their objections before filing suit. The lawsuit, brought by a Teamsters-affiliated pension fund, claimed Apple overvalued restricted stock units in 2021 and 2022.

summary: Nvidia briefly surpassed Amazon in market value, making it the fourth most valuable US-listed company earlier in the day. The chipmaker's rally, driven by exploding demand for AI chips, has seen its shares jump 46% this year. While Nvidia closed slightly below Amazon's valuation, the event marks a significant milestone fueled by the AI boom.

title: Meta settles lawsuit over haptic feedback tech in Quest headsets
summary: Immersion, a company specializing in haptic feedback technology, has settled a lawsuit with Meta over Meta's use of touch-feedback in its Quest VR headsets. The settlement involves Meta licensing Immersion's patents for its hardware, software, VR, and gaming products, though the terms were not disclosed. Immersion has a history of pursuing patent infringement lawsuits against major tech companies like Microsoft, Sony, Apple, and Valve.

title: Michael Burry Covers Bet Against Chips ETF, Buys Health and Tech Stocks
summary: Michael Burry's Scion Asset Management has changed its investment strategy, abandoning its bearish bet against semiconductor companies by closing its position against the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX). Instead, the firm nearly doubled its holdings to 25 positions, acquiring shares in health and technology sectors, and holds no bearish positions as of the end of 2023. Burry, known from "The Big Short," had previously bet against the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 indexes.

Investors should consider the implications of this concentration on future performance, especially in different economic scenarios like a soft landing.

title: Can Korea fend off China in display race?
summary: China is rapidly gaining on Korea in the display market, particularly in OLED technology for mobile phones, driven by state subsidies and technology transfers. While China has already surpassed Korea in LCDs, Korea is focusing on IT OLEDs and innovative TV features to maintain its competitive edge. Despite China's increasing market share in terms of volume, Korea still leads in sales value for premium displays.

summary: Stryker announced new advancements for its Mako surgical robotic platform, including the myMako app for Apple Vision Pro and iPhone and the Direct Anterior Reconstructive Technology (DART). These updates were showcased at AAOS in San Francisco, with further Mako expansions, including Mako Spine and Mako Shoulder, anticipated later in 2024.

This decision upholds a lower court's ruling which overturned the initial verdict.

summary: Walmart reported robust fourth-quarter results, driven by inflation-squeezed shoppers seeking value, performing better than rivals in a broad slowdown of discretionary spending. The company also announced a $2.3 billion acquisition of smart-TV maker Vizio, aiming to bolster its advertising business, Walmart Connect, and enhance its presence in consumers' homes. This strategic move aligns with Walmart's plan to diversify its profit streams, with a greater focus on advertising and online marketplace businesses in the coming years.

summary: Coherent has sold its gallium arsenide (GaAs) wafer fabrication facility in the north of England to the UK government for a reported £20 million. The move is part of Coherent's strategy to optimize its portfolio and streamline operations following the 2022 merger of II-VI and the original Coherent laser business. summary: A market research firm, Strategy Risks, has identified the most vulnerable US companies among the top 250 publicly listed firms regarding their exposure to China. title: Visa monopolizes debit card networks, DOJ lawsuit claims
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) has filed an antitrust lawsuit against Visa Inc., alleging the company maintains an unlawful monopoly on debit card networks. The lawsuit claims Visa engages in anticompetitive practices, such as penalizing banks and merchants using alternative payment systems and making agreements with technology companies like Apple, PayPal, and Square to prevent them from becoming competitors. These actions have allowed Visa to control over 60% of debit card transactions and charge more than $7 billion in processing fees, which the DOJ argues are passed on to consumers.

title: TSMC signs deal with US chip test firm
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) has partnered with Amkor Technology Inc to provide advanced packaging and test services in Arizona, supporting customer needs for geographical flexibility in chip manufacturing. This collaboration will establish local advanced packaging capabilities for TSMC's customers, especially those using its Phoenix, Arizona wafer fabrication facilities, and aims to strengthen the US semiconductor ecosystem. Amkor's planned facility in Peoria, Arizona, will be the largest outsourced advanced packaging and test facility in the US, with TSMC leveraging its services for technologies like Integrated Fan-Out (InFO) and Chip on Wafer on Substrate (CoWoS).

title: Amkor secured north Peoria land for its $2B complex. What's next?
summary: Amkor Technology Inc. has finalized the purchase of 56 acres in north Peoria for its $2 billion microchip assembly and testing facility, which will be the largest of its kind in the U.S. The project, supported by $600 million in CHIPS Act subsidies, aims to create about 2,000 jobs and will serve companies like Apple and TSMC. Construction is slated to begin by September 2025, with the first phase completed by September 2027 and full completion by September 2034.

title: E.l.f. brings shopping to the speakeasy with Virtual Luxe Lounge
summary: E.l.f. Cosmetics has introduced the "Virtual Luxe Lounge," an immersive 3D digital shopping experience accessible to members of its Beauty Squad loyalty program. Developed with Obsess, this speakeasy-themed platform allows users to shop holiday product drops and access exclusive coupons. This initiative is part of E.l.f.'s broader strategy to engage consumers digitally, following previous collaborations like a beauty shopping app for Apple Vision Pro, and aligns with their significant marketing investments that have boosted sales and attracted younger audiences.

title: Contact - The Lethbridge Herald - News and Sports from around Lethbridge
summary: Simplify Asset Management Inc. announced that its Simplify Stable Income ETF (NYSE Arca: BUCK) has been renamed the Simplify Treasury Option Income ETF. This change became effective on October 29, 2024. Simplify Asset Management, founded in 2020, specializes in options-based strategies to address portfolio challenges.

title: Apple Takes Over iCloud Passwords Add-On for Firefox
summary: Apple has officially taken over the independent iCloud Passwords add-on for Firefox, transitioning its ownership on addons.mozilla.org from developer Aurélien Garnier to Apple Inc. This move allows Firefox users running macOS Sonoma or recent Windows versions to confidently use Apple's password management features outside of Safari. While it's unclear if Apple acquired the code or hired Garnier, this step is seen as a positive expansion of iCloud Passwords support to non-Apple browsers and platforms, with potential future Windows support.

title: Masimo update: SEC announces investigation of RTW Investments and role in proxy war voting
summary: The SEC has launched an investigation into RTW Investments' role in Masimo's recent proxy war, specifically regarding an "empty voting" scheme. Masimo alleges that former CEO Joe Kiani and RTW conspired to manipulate shareholder votes, rigging 19% in Kiani's favor through practices like put options or selling shares after record dates. While empty voting is not inherently illegal, Masimo claims evidence of an insider group, which is a red flag for the SEC and potentially the Department of Justice.

title: Apple Expands Footprint at 11 Penn Plaza
summary: Apple has significantly expanded its footprint at 11 Penn Plaza in Midtown Manhattan, securing an additional 61,000 square feet and bringing its total occupancy to 460,000 square feet. This deal, a direct lease agreement with Vornado Realty Trust rather than a sublease from Macy's, allows Apple to occupy floors four through fourteen of the historic building. Despite Apple's expansion, Macy's remains the primary tenant and headquarters at 11 Penn Plaza.

title: The Inside Story of Apple Intelligence
summary: This article delves into Apple's strategy for generative AI, dubbed Apple Intelligence, highlighting the company's "best, not first" approach. Key executives, including John Giannandrea and Craig Federighi, explain that Apple has been preparing for this moment for years and focused on integrating AI at a systems level with a strong emphasis on privacy. The piece also contrasts Apple's approach with competitors and discusses the future trajectory of AI at Apple.

title: Apple plans three-year modem rollout to compete with Qualcomm, Bloomberg News reports
summary: Apple is preparing to launch its own series of cellular modem chips starting next year, aiming to replace components from Qualcomm by 2027. This move intensifies competition with Qualcomm, which currently supplies modems to Apple, and could impact other Apple suppliers like Skyworks Solutions and Qorvo. Apple has been developing its own modem technology since acquiring Intel's modem unit in 2019 and recently signed a deal with Broadcom for 5G radio frequency components.

title: BlackRock, Inc. Reduces Stake in iShares MSCI Poland ETF
summary: BlackRock, Inc. reduced its stake in the iShares MSCI Poland ETF (EPOL) by selling 880,171 shares on November 30, 2024, at $22.09 per share, leaving them with 133,296 shares. This move reflects a strategic adjustment by BlackRock, a leading investment firm with $4.761.03 trillion in equity and top holdings like Apple and Amazon. The iShares MSCI Poland ETF, with a market capitalization of $222.704 million, has shown a 4.48% price gain since the transaction and a 5.24% year-to-date appreciation, boasting a GF Score of 82/100 despite BlackRock's reduced position.

title: Report: Apple will ship custom 5G modem chip with the 2025 iPhone SE
summary: Apple Inc.'s custom 5G modem chip, codenamed Sinope, is expected to debut in the 2025 iPhone SE. Produced by TSMC, Sinope offers download speeds of up to 4 gigabits per second, which is less than half of Qualcomm's latest modems due to more limited frequency support and carrier aggregation implementation. Apple plans to integrate Sinope with its Carpo RF front end and aims to release more advanced custom modems in subsequent years, eventually hoping to outperform Qualcomm and integrate modems directly into iPhone processors, as well as extend their use to Macs and the Vision Pro.

title: E-mini Nasdaq-100 Futures - Volume & Open Interest
summary: CME Group highlights the E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures as a cost-effective and flexible way to gain market exposure to the Nasdaq-100 Index, covering 100 large-cap companies. The article emphasizes superior liquidity, leverage, and tax benefits compared to direct stock or ETF investments. It also provides tools, resources, and educational content for traders interested in these products.

title: NYC ad agencies Omnicom, Interpublic to form $30bn marketing powerhouse
summary: Omnicom is set to acquire Interpublic Group in a stock-for-stock deal, creating the world's largest advertising agency with combined annual revenue of almost $26bn and a market worth of over $30bn. The merger aims to accelerate innovation, leverage new technologies like AI, and achieve annual cost savings of $750m. The deal, which could face regulatory scrutiny, positions the combined entity, Omnicom, to better compete with tech giants and adapt to the evolving advertising landscape.

title: Big Advertising just got bigger with Omnicom’s Interpublic merger
summary: Omnicom Group has agreed to acquire Interpublic Group, aiming to create the world's largest advertising company, bringing together agencies for major brands like Apple, McDonald’s, and Pepsi. This merger seeks to accelerate innovation and leverage new technologies, expecting to generate $750 million in annual cost synergies and increase adjusted earnings per share for both companies. The move reflects the advertising holding company model's continuous evolution to keep pace with technology and client demands, while Omnicom also focuses on scaling AI efforts and maintaining agency brand independence.

summary: This page provides comprehensive information on the Invesco Top QQQ ETF (QBIG), including its current stock price, trading exchange, and key financial statistics. It also features performance data, holdings breakdown, company profile, and news related to the ETF, along with technical analysis insights.

title: Apple to bring e-commerce site, stores to Saudi Arabia
summary: Apple is expanding its retail presence in Saudi Arabia, launching an online Apple Store in summer 2025 with Arabic service and support. Following this, the tech giant plans to open its first flagship physical stores in the kingdom starting in 2026, including a notable location in Diriyah. This expansion builds on existing investments, such as the Apple Developer Academy, and aims to deepen connections with Saudi Arabian customers.

title: Taiwan Semiconductor Extends Lead As Top Chipmaker
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) has solidified its position as the top global wafer foundry, increasing its market share to 64.9% in Q3 2024 due to strong demand for smartphone products and high-performance computing. The company reported $23.5 billion in revenue, a 39% increase, driven by 3nm and 5nm technologies. This growth contrasts with Samsung's market share decline and highlights the rising demand for advanced chip technologies and the impact of U.S. chip subsidies on key players like TSM and GlobalFoundries.

title: Franklin Resources Inc. Reduces Stake in ClearBridge Energy Mids
summary: Franklin Resources Inc. has significantly reduced its stake in ClearBridge Energy Midstream Opportunity Fund Inc. (EMO) by 55.24%, selling 40,610 shares at $47.6 per share. This move leaves Franklin Resources with 0.26% of its portfolio in EMO, signaling a strategic adjustment based on EMO's declining stock price and poor potential for future performance despite its focus on high cash distributions. The transaction highlights Franklin Resources' conservative investment philosophy and focus on optimizing its $353.59 billion equity portfolio.

title: T. Rowe Price PM a ‘big believer’ in crypto
summary: Dominic Rizzo, manager of T. Rowe Price’s new technology-focused ETF, expresses strong belief in crypto, DeFi, and stablecoins for their long-term potential applications. He notes that currently, Coinbase is one of the few ways for public market equity investors to gain exposure to these trends, fitting his investment framework which includes being a "linchpin technology" in a secular growth market with improving fundamentals and reasonable valuation. Rizzo anticipates more crypto equity opportunities will emerge eventually and his firm aims to stay informed regarding this significant trend.

title: Jefferies says the Russell 2000 will reach 2,715 by 2025 year-end (NYSEARCA:IWM)
summary: Jefferies analysts predict the Russell 2000 will increase by 13.5% to 2,715 by the end of 2025, anticipating it will finally outperform large-cap stocks after eight years of underperformance. Steven DeSanctis, Jefferies' U.S. small-mid cap strategist, provided this outlook.

title: Apple honors 2024 App Store Award winners
summary: Apple announced the winners of the 2024 App Store Awards, recognizing 17 apps and games for their exceptional user experiences, design, and innovation. The awards include categories for various Apple devices, the inaugural Apple Vision Pro category, and Cultural Impact winners, highlighting developers who have enriched users' lives and communities. The winning selections showcase the diverse opportunities available across the App Store and the Apple ecosystem.

title: Should You Invest in the Fidelity MSCI Information Technology Index ETF (FTEC)?
summary: This article evaluates the Fidelity MSCI Information Technology Index ETF (FTEC) as an investment option for broad exposure to the Technology - Broad sector. It highlights FTEC's passive management, low expense ratio (0.08%), and strong year-to-date performance (up 31.10%). summary: This article highlights three Vanguard ETFs—the S&P 500 ETF (VOO), Growth ETF (VUG), and Total Bond Market ETF (BND)—as key components for building a balanced, long-term investment portfolio. It emphasizes Vanguard's low-cost structure and passively managed funds as an effective wealth-building strategy. The article provides insights into each ETF's performance, holdings, and expense ratios, along with a revised framework for age-based asset allocation.

title: Fatal mistake that turned Kodak from a $31,000,000,000 photography company to bankrupt
summary: This article details the downfall of Kodak, once a $31 billion photography giant, that ultimately led to its bankruptcy. The company's fatal error was its reluctance to embrace digital photography, despite an employee inventing the first handheld digital camera in 1975, because it prioritized profitable film sales. Although Kodak later tried to enter the digital market, it was too late and faced intense competition, low profit margins, and financial struggles, eventually filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2012.

title: Match Group Warns Negative Currency Impacts Will Bring Down Revenue
summary: Match Group announced that unfavorable currency exchange rates will cause its current-quarter revenue to be below earlier estimates, reducing fourth-quarter revenue by $15 million more than anticipated, primarily impacting Tinder. The company also noted that Tinder's new user declines on Apple iOS have not fully recovered, though it did announce an additional $1.5 billion in stock buybacks. Match Group shares fell over 5% on the news and are down about 14% year-to-date.

summary: This article details the top holdings of the Zacks Focus Growth ETF (GROZ), which primarily invests in large-cap North American companies. title: Report: Apple working with Broadcom to develop custom chipset for AI
summary: Apple Inc. is reportedly collaborating with Broadcom Inc. to develop a custom server processor, codenamed “Baltra,” for AI features in its iOS operating system, with a targeted launch in 2026. This move aligns with Apple's strategy of using proprietary chips for on-device AI and Broadcom's expertise in semiconductor interconnect designs. The project likely leverages Broadcom's advanced packaging technologies for faster chip-to-chip communications.

title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) is favoured by institutional owners who hold 61% of the company
summary: Institutional investors hold 61% of Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL), making them the most powerful shareholder group with significant influence on the company's share price. The Vanguard Group, Inc. is the largest shareholder with 8.9% of shares, while insiders own less than 1% and the general public holds a 37% stake.

title: 6 Best Ways to Redeem Aeroplan Points
summary: This article by NerdWallet Canada outlines six effective strategies for maximizing the value of Aeroplan points. Key recommendations include understanding the average point value, considering partner airlines for better redemption rates, opting for business-class flights, identifying "sweet spot" routes, utilizing family sharing plans, and prioritizing flight redemptions over other options like gift cards or car rentals. The article emphasizes calculating the cents-per-point value to ensure worthwhile redemptions.

title: Broadcom ETFs Surge on Strong AI Demand
summary: Broadcom's shares surged by 20% following strong earnings and optimistic projections for its AI business, pushing its market cap past $1 trillion. This surge significantly boosted ETFs with large Broadcom holdings, such as the Defiance Daily Target 2X Long AVGO ETF (AVGX) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX). The demand for Broadcom's custom AI chips, favored by major tech companies like Alphabet, Meta, and Apple, is seen as a key driver for its continued growth.

title: Sonos Arc Ultra review: The best Dolby Atmos soundbar just got better
summary: The Sonos Arc Ultra soundbar aims to redeem the brand after a problematic app rollout. It significantly upgrades over its predecessor with a 9.1.4-channel configuration, Sound Motion technology for improved audio quality in a more compact design, and Bluetooth support. While a substantial upgrade for new buyers seeking premium home theater sound, current Sonos Arc owners may not find the improvements significant enough to warrant replacement.

title: TSMC says first advanced U.S. chip plant 'dang near back' on schedule. Here's an inside look at the Arizona fab
summary: TSMC's first advanced U.S. chip fabrication plant in Arizona is "dang near back on the original schedule" after delays and an increased investment from $12 billion to $20 billion. The plant will produce 4-nanometer chips and has committed to building two more fabs by the end of the decade, totaling $65 billion. Challenges include securing a skilled workforce, managing significant water and power demands, and global supply chain complexities, but the U.S. Commerce Department finalized $6.6 billion in CHIPS Act funding for the project.

title: Liberty All-Star Growth Fund Delivers Stellar 8.7% Monthly Return, YTD Gains Exceed 20% with Tech-Heavy Portfolio
summary: The Liberty All-Star Growth Fund (ASG) reported robust performance for November 2024, with its Net Asset Value (NAV) increasing by 8.72% and its market price by 7.73%. Year-to-date, the fund's NAV rose by 20.25% and its market price by 21.05%. The fund maintains a technology-heavy portfolio, with top holdings including NVIDIA, Apple, and Amazon, and primarily invests in Information Technology.

title: Broadcom's AI Chip Leadership Puts Pressure on Nvidia and Marvell, Analysts Say
summary: Broadcom's stock surged after reporting strong Q4 adjusted EPS results and raising its dividend, driven by its leadership in AI custom Application-Specific Integrated Circuits (ASICs). Analysts upgraded Broadcom's price targets, highlighting its expanding AI opportunities and advanced 3nm silicon technology, which puts it ahead of competitors like Nvidia and Marvell. The company anticipates significant growth in its AI revenues, expecting to reach $30 billion by calendar 2027 based on strong demand from hyperscalers.

title: Will the iShares S&P 500 ETF (IVV) return another 36% in 2025?
summary: The article discusses the extraordinary 36.34% year-to-date return of the iShares S&P 500 ETF (IVV) in 2024, largely driven by the "magnificent seven" big tech stocks. It explores whether this strong performance is sustainable for 2025, referencing an expert's bullish outlook on US equities due to anticipated earnings growth, healthy economic projections, and falling inflation. The expert suggests that the high valuations of the big tech companies are justified by strong fundamentals.

title: 11%+ Yields From AI Stocks: QQQI Vs. QYLD (NASDAQ:QQQI)
summary: This article compares QQQI and QYLD, two funds designed to generate high yields from mega-cap AI companies, to help income-focused investors choose a suitable diversification instrument. While mega-cap tech stocks typically offer low dividends, these funds aim to provide attractive income opportunities. The analysis details their characteristics and suitability for an income portfolio, recommending that interested investors can access further insights through High Yield Investor's service.

title: A new investment fund is saying ‘no’ to DEI-focused companies — and ‘yes’ to others
summary: Azoria, a new investment firm, is launching an ETF that will exclude S&P 500 companies with explicit racial and gender hiring targets. The firm believes companies hiring based on skill and ability will financially outperform those focused on DEI, citing examples like Best Buy and the underperformance of DEI-focused companies. Azoria aims to provide investors with a meritocracy-rooted alternative, investing in companies that abandon such hiring practices.

title: Invesco launches ETF to maximize on the tech concentration craze
summary: Invesco has launched a new exchange-traded fund, the Invesco Top QQQ ETF (QBIG), designed to provide investors with exposure to the top 45% of companies within the Nasdaq-100 Index. This move by Invesco, known for its large Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), aims to meet investor demand for capturing the megacap concentration story within the Nasdaq, with initial top holdings including Apple, Nvidia, and Microsoft. The launch reflects a broader trend of new funds emerging to address market enthusiasm for or aversion to megacap exposure.

title: Charted: Magnificent 7 Market Cap as a Share of the S&P 500
summary: This article examines the increasing share of the S&P 500's market capitalization held by the "Magnificent 7" stocks over the past decade. It highlights that these seven stocks have grown by nearly 800% in market cap, reaching almost 35% of the S&P 500 by mid-2024, raising concerns about potential over-exposure for investors.

title: Victoria’s Secret Is PETA’s ‘Company of the Year’ for its Fabulously Innovative Feather-Free Fashion Show
summary: PETA has named Victoria’s Secret its 2024 Company of the Year for its innovative use of feather-free materials in its fashion show, showcasing vegan Angel wings made from 3-D printed materials, quilted satin, soda can tabs, and Swarovski crystals. This decision followed PETA's communication with the retailer about the cruelty involved in obtaining feathers from birds. The move is applauded by PETA as an example for designers and consumers to adopt animal-friendly practices in fashion.

title: Pattern Energy Announces Equity Investment from Consortium Headed by APG and ART
summary: Pattern Energy announced that a consortium led by APG Asset Management and Australian Retirement Trust will acquire Riverstone Holdings LLC’s equity stake in the company. This investment strengthens Pattern Energy's position, allowing it to advance its development pipeline of over 25-gigawatts of renewable energy and transmission projects. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2025.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Leveraged ETFs Offer Short-Term Edge As Traders Eye Semiconductors, China, And Quantum Tech In Post-Election Market
summary: Traders are increasingly leveraging ETFs to capitalize on short-term market opportunities, especially after recent elections. Analysts from Direxion and The Mercator LLC highlighted strategies in semiconductors due to AI and quantum computing advancements, and in Chinese markets following stimulus measures. Single-stock ETFs are also gaining popularity for tactical trading in high-profile companies, though experts caution on understanding their short-term nature and daily rebalancing effects.

title: ABFL Top Holdings List & Exposure (Abacus FCF Leaders ETF)
summary: This article provides a detailed list of the top holdings for the Abacus FCF Leaders ETF (ABFL), including company names, weights, and shares held. It also breaks down ABFL's geographic, currency, sector, and industry exposures. The ETF's top holdings are NVIDIA, Apple, and Mastercard, with its largest exposure to the United States and the Technology sector.

title: Apple says it has told suppliers to stop buying minerals from Congo
summary: Apple has instructed its suppliers to halt the purchase of tin, tantalum, tungsten, and gold from the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda due to escalating conflict in the region. This decision comes in response to allegations from the Congolese government that Apple uses conflict minerals laundered through international supply chains. Apple strongly disputes these allegations.

title: Your next TV won’t be micro-LED. Here’s why
summary: The article explains why micro-LED TVs, despite their stunning visual quality, are unlikely to become mainstream consumer technology soon. The primary challenges are the extreme difficulty and cost associated with manufacturing them at smaller, consumer-friendly sizes, mainly due to pixel pitch and heat management issues. The author suggests that electroluminescent quantum dots (QDEL) and quantum dot micro-LEDs are more promising future display technologies, while PHOLED offers an evolutionary, rather than revolutionary, advancement.

title: Apple Supplier Jabil Soars On Q1 Earnings Beat Fueled By Data Center Demand: Retail Gets Bullish
summary: Jabil Inc., an Apple supplier, saw its shares jump by 10% after reporting first-quarter results that exceeded Wall Street expectations. The strong performance was driven by robust demand in its intelligent infrastructure segment, particularly in cloud, data center, and warehouse automation markets, leading to an "extremely bullish" retail sentiment. Despite an overall revenue decline due to a business transition, the company provided an optimistic outlook for Q2 2025 and the full fiscal year.

title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) is a favorite amongst institutional investors who own 61%
summary: Institutional investors own 61% of Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL), making it a favored stock among this group. While this signifies credibility, the concentration of ownership among a few large investors means their trading actions can significantly impact the stock price. Insiders, despite owning less than 1%, hold a substantial dollar value in shares and have been recent sellers.

title: After Earnings, Is Broadcom Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Broadcom's third-quarter earnings report, released on December 12, 2024, has led Morningstar to raise its fair value estimate for the company's stock to $190 per share, up from $155, driven by an increased AI revenue growth forecast. Despite the upward revision, Morningstar now considers Broadcom's shares to be roughly fairly valued after a significant post-earnings jump, giving it a 2-star rating. The article highlights Broadcom's strong potential in AI chips, its wide economic moat from intangible assets and switching costs, and its financial strength, while also noting risks related to market cycles and supply chain reliance on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing.

title: JEPQ vs. QQQ: Which ETF Aligns With Your Investment Goals?
summary: This article compares two ETFs, JEPQ and QQQ, both tied to the Nasdaq 100, highlighting their distinct investment strategies. JEPQ focuses on income generation and reduced volatility through covered call strategies, offering a 9.2% annual yield, while QQQ provides direct exposure to the Nasdaq 100 with a focus on growth and higher volatility. The analysis delves into their historical performance, risk metrics, income stability, and suitability for different investment goals, concluding that JEPQ is better for income-seekers and QQQ for growth-oriented investors.

title: Jabil’s Winning Streak Begins: Market Bottom Set, Future in Focus
summary: Jabil's fiscal Q1 2025 report indicates that the company has hit its market bottom, with a strong outlook for future growth despite a top-line contraction. The company outperformed expectations for both revenue and earnings, providing optimistic guidance and benefiting from strength in cloud, data center, and digital commerce segments. Analyst and institutional investor trends are positive, supporting a potential new all-time high for the stock.

title: ‘Synaptics plans to assemble 10% chips in India’
summary: US semiconductor company Synaptics Inc. plans to assemble and package 10% of its chips in India by 2027 to diversify its supply chain and reduce reliance on China. The company will use an OSAT facility in Hyderabad and partner with embed UR to develop edge AI solutions, aiming for the process to begin in late 2025 or early 2026. This move also addresses concerns about proposed US tariffs and the need for supply chain alternatives.

title: Analyst says Celestica’s momentum has ‘continued’ through the year
summary: Robert Young, managing director at Canada Canaccord Genuity, highlights Celestica's strong performance, attributing it to conservative guidance and a "beat and raise cadence." The company's significant business with top hyper scalers, including Google and Meta, for designing networking gear and AI servers, is a major growth driver. Young notes that Celestica is increasingly recognized for its higher-value OEM role due to its IP, moving beyond its traditional EMS vendor perception.

title: The 'boring' department store whose stock is outperforming Tesla
summary: Dillard's, a regional department store, has seen its stock outperform Tesla, Apple, and Microsoft over the last five years, with a 500% increase. This success is attributed to its "drama-free consistency," focus on business fundamentals, supplier and employee loyalty, and a strategy of avoiding constant discounting. Dillard's has also been surprisingly tech-focused, adopting real-time sales and inventory tracking earlier than rivals, leading activist investor Barington Capital to suggest Macy's emulate its model.

title: Corsair K65 Plus Apple Edition Review: Just Buy the Non-Apple Version
summary: The Corsair K65 Plus Apple Edition keyboard is functionally identical to the standard version but costs more due to its Apple-exclusive colorways. While it offers excellent pre-lubed linear switches ideal for gaming and good build quality, its custom RGB lighting and key remapping features are limited in wireless modes. The reviewer recommends opting for the standard black version as it frequently goes on sale and provides the same performance without the inflated price of the Apple-exclusive model.

title: Apple looks to make a splash in 2025 with AI-infused smart home devices
summary: Apple is set to launch an AI-powered smart home hub in 2025 with a 6-inch display and new operating system, alongside upgrades to existing Home devices. The company is also developing an in-home security camera and a smart doorbell with advanced facial recognition, leveraging its commitment to privacy to gain consumer trust and expand revenue in the smart home market. These new offerings signal a significant push by Apple into the connected home ecosystem.

title: Apple to see strong Christmas iPhone sales that launch a ‘renaissance of growth’
summary: Apple is projected to experience a renaissance of growth driven by strong iPhone sales during the holiday season, fueled by an estimated 300 million iPhones over four years old. This potential "supercycle" is expected to lead to significant upgrades to new AI-capable iPhones, especially in the key China market, and could propel Apple to a $4 trillion market cap.

title: Apple approaches $4 trillion valuation as investors bet on AI momentum
summary: Apple is nearing a $4 trillion market valuation, driven by investor enthusiasm for its AI enhancements, which are expected to boost iPhone sales. The company has outpaced Nvidia and Microsoft in this race, with a roughly 16% share jump since November adding about $500 billion to its market cap. Analysts anticipate a rebound in iPhone revenue in 2025 as Apple integrates generative AI technology across its devices.

title: Globalstar director James Monroe III buys $985k in stock By Investing.com
summary: Globalstar director James Monroe III has purchased 500,000 shares of the company's common stock for approximately $985,050. This acquisition comes as Globalstar shows strong momentum with an 87.5% price return over the past six months and reported record Q3 revenue, alongside strategic advancements in 5G technology and satellite connectivity with Apple. The company has also announced plans for a reverse stock split to optimize its capital structure.

title: Evolving the device experience at Microsoft
summary: Microsoft is transitioning its employee device management from a traditional on-premises model to a modern, cloud-based approach using Microsoft Intune, Azure Active Directory, and co-management strategies. This shift supports hybrid work, enables employees to be productive from anywhere on various devices (Windows, Android, iOS, macOS), and enhances security through Zero Trust principles and verified device health. The migration addresses challenges by using Hybrid Azure AD joined devices as a bridge and standardizing management practices.

title: Apple’s been on an uncommonly strong run. So a tough January could now be in the cards.
summary: Apple's stock has achieved a rare five-week streak of 2%-plus gains, a phenomenon that historically precedes a roughly 5% drop in the following month. Investors are advised to be cautious as this pattern suggests a potentially tough January for Apple shares. The stock's recent performance marks the first time in 14 years and very rarely in the company's 44-year public history that it has had such a strong, sustained run.

title: Why Samsung and LG may be the reason Apple delaying the all-screen iPhone
summary: Apple's plan for an all-screen iPhone has been delayed past 2026, reportedly due to technical challenges faced by display manufacturers Samsung Display and LG Display. They are struggling with developing thin film encapsulation for OLEDs and suitable optical clear adhesives, pushing the potential release to 2027 or later. Apple aims for a bezel-free design that avoids the "magnifying glass effect" seen in other curved-screen phones.

title: Jim Cramer on Apple Inc. (AAPL): ‘It Was The Dumb Money That Was Getting Out, Because Warren Buffett Or One Of His Assistants Made Us Nervous’
summary: Jim Cramer discussed Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) within the context of AI stocks and overall market performance in 2024. He highlighted that "dumb money" sold off Apple shares due to investor nervousness, potentially influenced by Warren Buffett, despite strong underlying sales. Cramer also offered trading advice for 2025, emphasizing the importance of not getting intoxicated by gains, having the fortitude to hold stocks during tough times, and carefully staging buy orders.

title: Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) Poised for Strong 2025 Growth with Custom AI Chips and Strategic Partnerships, Says William Blair
summary: Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) is anticipated to experience strong growth in 2025, driven by its custom AI chip development and strategic partnerships with major cloud customers, according to William Blair. The company recently surpassed a $1 trillion market cap and its CEO announced the development of custom AI chips with three large cloud clients. William Blair maintains an Outperform rating, expecting steady growth from existing partnerships and potential new clients like ByteDance, OpenAI, and Apple.

title: Growth ETFs Shaken Up as Tech Takes on Value Blush
summary: Growth ETFs like IVW are undergoing significant rebalancing as major tech companies such as Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, and Adobe are no longer considered pure growth stocks by S&P Global. This reclassification means investors will see a smaller allocation to these tech giants in growth ETFs and a larger presence of financial firms like Berkshire Hathaway and JPMorgan Chase, which are now being given a "growth blush". The rebalancing also shifts tech's share in the S&P Value Index significantly, with these companies now having their weightings divided between growth and value characteristics based on S&P's multifactor analysis.

title: Corsair Gaming Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2024 Financial Results
summary: Corsair Gaming announced its financial results for Q4 and full year 2024, reporting solid Q4 revenue and adjusted EBITDA driven by strong growth in the Gamer and Creator Peripherals segment.
